theory.intro: To find a perimeter you need every side length. In many shapes, some sides are equal, so a missing length can be worked out from the ones you are given.
facts: A **rectangle** has opposite sides equal — you only need one length and one width.
A **square** has all four sides equal — you only need one side.
If a side is not marked, look for an equal side that **is** marked.
steps: Identify the shape and which sides are equal.
Use a marked side to find any equal unmarked side.
Add all the side lengths once you know them.

foundation.question_text:
Which labelled side lengths are needed to calculate this rectangle's perimeter?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(A)at(0,0);\coordinate(B)at(5,0);\coordinate(C)at(5,3);\coordinate(D)at(0,3);\draw(A)--(B)node[midway,below]{$a$};\draw(B)--(C)node[midway,right]{$b$};\draw(C)--(D);\draw(D)--(A);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so one length and one width are enough.
Needed: $a$ and $b$

foundation.question_text:
How many side lengths must be measured to find this square's perimeter?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\draw(0,0)--(4,0)--(4,4)--(0,4)--cycle;\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
All four sides of a square are equal, so only one side length is needed.
Answer: $1$

foundation.question_text:
Which labelled side lengths are needed to calculate this triangle's perimeter?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(A)at(0,0);\coordinate(B)at(5,0);\coordinate(C)at(2,3.5);\draw(A)--(B)node[midway,below]{$p$};\draw(B)--(C)node[midway,above right]{$q$};\draw(C)--(A)node[midway,above left]{$r$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
No sides are marked equal, so every side is needed.
Needed: $p$, $q$ and $r$

foundation.question_text:
How many side lengths must be measured to find this rhombus's perimeter?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\draw(0,0)--(4,0)--(5.5,2.5)--(1.5,2.5)--cycle;\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
All four sides of a rhombus are equal, so one side length is enough.
Answer: $1$

foundation.question_text:
Which labelled side lengths are needed to calculate this parallelogram's perimeter?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(A)at(0,0);\coordinate(B)at(5,0);\coordinate(C)at(6.5,2.5);\coordinate(D)at(1.5,2.5);\draw(A)--(B)node[midway,below]{$m$};\draw(B)--(C)node[midway,right]{$n$};\draw(C)--(D);\draw(D)--(A);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so one side from each pair is needed.
Needed: $m$ and $n$

foundation.question_text:
Which labelled side lengths are needed to calculate this irregular quadrilateral's perimeter?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\coordinate(A)at(0,0);\coordinate(B)at(5,0);\coordinate(C)at(4,3);\coordinate(D)at(1,4);\draw(A)--(B)node[midway,below]{$a$};\draw(B)--(C)node[midway,right]{$b$};\draw(C)--(D)node[midway,above]{$c$};\draw(D)--(A)node[midway,left]{$d$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
No equal-side information is given, so all four side lengths are needed.
Needed: $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$

development.question_text:
A rectangle has its top and bottom both labelled, but no vertical side measured. Is there enough information for its perimeter?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\draw(0,0)--(5,0)node[midway,below]{$8\text{ m}$};\draw(5,0)--(5,3);\draw(5,3)--(0,3)node[midway,above]{$8\text{ m}$};\draw(0,3)--(0,0);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text: No. Both labels give the same length. One vertical side length is still needed.

development.question_text:
A square has two adjacent sides labelled $6\text{ cm}$. Which measurement is unnecessary?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\draw(0,0)--(4,0)node[midway,below]{$6\text{ cm}$};\draw(4,0)--(4,4)node[midway,right]{$6\text{ cm}$};\draw(4,4)--(0,4);\draw(0,4)--(0,0);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text: Either label is unnecessary because one side determines all four sides of a square.

development.question_text:
An isosceles triangle has two equal sloping sides. Which measurements are sufficient for its perimeter?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\usetikzlibrary{decorations.markings}\tikzset{tickmark/.style={postaction={decorate,decoration={markings,mark=at position 0.5 with {\draw(0pt,-4pt)--(0pt,4pt);}}}}}\coordinate(A)at(0,0);\coordinate(B)at(5,0);\coordinate(C)at(2.5,4);\draw(A)--(B)node[midway,below]{$b$};\draw[tickmark](B)--(C)node[midway,above right]{$s$};\draw[tickmark](C)--(A);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text: The base $b$ and one sloping side $s$ are sufficient because the other sloping side equals $s$.

development.question_text:
A regular hexagon has one side measured. How many additional side measurements are needed?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\foreach \i in {0,...,5}{\coordinate(P\i)at({60*\i}:2.5);}\draw(P0)--(P1)node[midway,above right]{$4\text{ cm}$};\draw(P1)--(P2)--(P3)--(P4)--(P5)--cycle;\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text:
A regular hexagon has six equal sides. The one measurement gives every side.
Additional measurements: $0$
Measure either vertical side, $BC$ or $AD$. One width plus the given length is sufficient.

development.question_text:
A kite has two pairs of equal adjacent sides. Which labelled lengths are sufficient?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]\usetikzlibrary{decorations.markings}\tikzset{tickmark/.style={postaction={decorate,decoration={markings,mark=at position 0.5 with {\draw(0pt,-4pt)--(0pt,4pt);}}}},tickmark2/.style={postaction={decorate,decoration={markings,mark=at position 0.5 with {\draw(-2pt,-4pt)--(-2pt,4pt);\draw(2pt,-4pt)--(2pt,4pt);}}}}}\coordinate(A)at(0,4);\coordinate(B)at(2.5,1);\coordinate(C)at(0,-3);\coordinate(D)at(-2.5,1);\draw[tickmark](A)--(B)node[midway,above right]{$u$};\draw[tickmark2](B)--(C)node[midway,below right]{$v$};\draw[tickmark2](C)--(D);\draw[tickmark](D)--(A);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text:
One length from each tick-mark family is required.
Needed: $u$ and $v$

mastery.question_text: A rectangle has side labels $12\text{ m}$, $7\text{ m}$ and $12\text{ m}$. Which label can be removed without losing enough information to find the perimeter?
mastery.solution_text: The repeated $12\text{ m}$ label can be removed. One $12\text{ m}$ side and the $7\text{ m}$ side determine both pairs.

mastery.question_text: A regular octagon and a scalene triangle are to have their perimeters calculated. What is the minimum total number of side measurements needed?
mastery.solution_text:
Regular octagon: $1$ measurement
Scalene triangle: $3$ measurements
Total: $4$ measurements

mastery.question_text: A parallelogram has only one long side measured. Explain exactly what additional measurement is needed.
mastery.solution_text: Measure one short side. Opposite sides are equal, so one long-side length and one short-side length determine all four sides.
